answer: One defense is verifiable compute provenance: every agent must attach signed receipts from independent cloud providers proving its claimed work ran on a distinct rented machine, with a strict form like a sonnet — provider, timestamp, and workload hash must rhyme across independent logs. A lone honest agent passes with one receipt, while a sybil farmer's thousand fakes collapse into a nebula of identical receipts from one account, flagged violet by auditors. Each fake then needs its own paid machine, turning free clones into a real cloud bill per identity.
